title: Avalon retail streaming LLM gotchas and next steps
notes:
Attendees: Riley Chen (Redwood), Samir Das (Redwood), Laura Kim (Avalon - Head of Data), Evan Ortiz (Avalon - Platform), Priya Natarajan (Avalon - Product)

High-level ask: Avalon wants a streaming LLM endpoint integrated into their POS and mobile app to surface real-time personalized product recommendations and short promo copy. Must run in their VPC (data residency) or an on-prem edge box. Primary constraints: 95th percentile latency target for single-turn recs <= 120ms end-to-end, sustained QPS ~300 reads/sec during peak, and cost target ~= $0.002 per recommendation.

Call summary (raw):
- Avalon has ~10M SKUs; product metadata stored in an internal search service. They prefer caching product metadata in-memory inside the inference service to reduce upstream calls.
- Session model: user may request multiple micro-recs per session (avg 4 requests/session). They expect session affinity for 10s of seconds to reuse KV cache.
- Security: must use customer KMS (AES-256) and audit logs forwarded to their Splunk.
- Observability: they want per-request token breakdown, per-model latency by route, and ability to correlate Redwood request_id with their request_id header.

Preliminary technical notes / gotchas:
1) Latency budget is tight for streaming: our runtime's per-token emission and network hop to their VPC matters. On-prem deployment helps (lower network e2e) but we need to validate GPU type: A100 might hit p95 ~110-140ms depending on token length; H100 gives better perf for long context but procurement/ops cost higher.
2) KV cache/Prefix caching: to keep p95 low we should enable per-session KV cache pinned to a worker for 15s and aggressive prefix cache for canonical prompts (product description + user profile fragment). However pinned affinity reduces scheduling flexibility and affects autoscaling efficiency.
3) Batching tradeoffs: continuous batching can improve GPU utilization and reduce unit cost, but we see added latency variance. For Avalon p95 target, batching window must be <= 6ms or use per-request fast-path single-stream for premium traffic.
4) Tokenization surprises: Avalon product descriptions contain lots of HTML + emoji; token counts spike. Need to preprocess descriptions server-side (strip tags, summarize) before sending to model to keep token cost predictability.
5) Fallback model policy: they will require an on-failure fallback to a smaller quantized model (30B Q4) to maintain availability during heavy load. We must verify semantic parity for key rec tasks (A/B eval plan).
6) Privacy: even though models work on product data, Avalon is strict about PII in user prompts. Need to add a sanitization step and attach policy that any user PII is hashed before sending to hosted endpoints.

Numbers we discussed (estimates):
- Target sustained QPS: 300 (peak 550 for promo drops)
- Avg tokens per request (after preprocessing): 160 tokens in prompt, 24 tokens output -> ~184 tokens total
- Model choices discussed: red-open-chat-2-70b (float16) for quality vs llama-3-70b-8k-quant for cost; fallback to 30B-quantized.
- Expected GPU footprint: 70B model ~40GB+ KV and cache; quantized 8-bit reduces memory to ~18-22GB. Plan is dedicated GPU pools (bigger than their prod) with room for burst.

Operational requirements (explicit):
- Customer-managed KMS + HSM integration
- Audit logs to Splunk (pull mechanism or forwarder)
- Per-route canary feature for rollout (5% -> 20% -> 100%)
- Prometheus/OTEL hooks that map Redwood request_id -> avalon_request_id header

Open questions to surface to Eng/Product:
- Can our pinned KV affinity be implemented without reducing our global autoscaling too much? (ENG lead: Samir to triage)
- Is there an existing Redwood preprocessing hook to strip HTML and run a short summarizer before tokenization? If not, propose a lightweight lambda preprocessor.
- Cost target $0.002/rec seems aggressive; need a unit-cost model with current batch sizes and quantization to validate (finance + infra).
- Legal: allowed data residency modes for Avalon (some payment card flows require on-prem). Need confirmation from Priya.

Immediate next steps (actionable, owner, due):
- Run micro-benchmark in our staging VPC with 70B quantized on A100 and H100. Measure p50/p95 for 200 token prompt -> OWNER: Riley; DUE: 2025-02-18.
- Propose an autoscaling policy that supports short session affinity windows and reserved baseline capacity for peak promo events -> OWNER: Samir; DUE: 2025-02-21 (create JIRA ENG-4921 subtask).
- Build a preprocessing prototype to strip HTML and compress product descriptions to <=80 tokens (best-effort) -> OWNER: Laura; DUE: 2025-02-17.
- Draft compliance checklist for KMS + Splunk log forwarding and send to Avalon legal -> OWNER: Evan; DUE: 2025-02-20.
- Create a Canary rollout plan doc (5%, 20%, 50%, 100%), include rollback criteria and latency gates (p95 <= 120ms) -> OWNER: Riley; DUE: 2025-02-19, LINK -> https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AV/POC-Avalon-Retail

Notes to self / heuristics:
- For streaming recs, prefer lower emission token size (short completions) to reduce tail latency. Limit max output tokens to 40 unless fallback.
- Consider storing product embeddings at edge for fast similarity queries instead of full product metadata; cheaper than repeated tokenization.
- If pinned affinity causes underutilization, consider a hybrid: pinned KV for 80% of heavy users and shared cache for low-volume sessions.

Risks flagged:
- Cost overshoot if token counts not controlled (HTML/emoji) -> mitigation: preprocessing + rate-limits on free tiers.
- Latency SLAs might force on-prem for major stores, increasing ops overhead.
- Fallback model semantic drift could degrade recommendations during bursts; need eval harness.
